title: The Placebo Effect: How Belief Rewires the Body
question: How can an inert pill or a fake procedure produce real, measurable physiological change?
summary: A sugar pill can ease pain, calm nausea, and even trigger dopamine release in the brain if the person taking it expects it to work. The placebo effect is not "nothing happening" — it is expectation and context reaching down into measurable biology, and it is reshaping how medicine understands the line between mind and body.
